## Cannot Fit a Tomb-level Model

-   **Small number of tombs**: Amfissa and 7 tombs from Elateia
-   For too many parameters: length of use, # analysed individuals, effect of 4 types of skeletal elements


$\Rightarrow$ **With the available data, a meaningful tomb-level model is not possible**

**Can still summarize and visualize the data.**

## Evidence against MNI-based inference

**Note**

With the tomb-level model out of the question, whether we use MNI-based or sample-based inference is irrelevant to our methodology.\
The only difference is how to interpret those results.

## Evidence against MNI-based inference

-   **The assumption is acknowledged as a simplification**\
    [Royal Society B article](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rstb/article/376/1816/20190719/31363/Sometimeshidden-but-always-there-the-assumptions)

    (c) Sampling bias

-   **Kinship determines burial context**\
    [Science article](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aax6219)

-   **Burial context determines preservation**\
    [JSTOR article](https://www.jstor.org/stable/280601)

**True Kinship -\> Burial context -\> Preservation -\> Data quality -\> Being sampled -\> Observed kinship**\

$\Rightarrow$ Can not work with the assumption that kinship is not independent of the preservation/sampling

$\Rightarrow$ Have to clearly state in the report as a limitation


## Why quality variables are excluded

-   The preservation bias is already taken care of from when we apply 15k threshold
-   Adding them (skeletal element & OSNP) would not contribute anything further to the model but would only make the numerical fitting process harder
